resources.string: Fatigue from high-force work, whole-body load, specific muscles, high-speed movements, and reactive movements is tracked on separate axes.
Early on, limited personal history may make the results less informative.
Check whether strength and badminton training are becoming overly concentrated in particular body areas or training objectives.
Interpret it as a signal that load has accumulated above your recent level, while also considering how you actually perform and whether you have pain or instability.
Analysis results are not absolute assessments of your health. They are information for tracking fatigue and training-load trends within your own workout history.
Local-muscle analysis prioritizes muscles with the highest current residual fatigue.
Open the guide to reading analysis results
Combines the five fatigue axes to show your overall current training-load state.
See where joint, tendon, ligament, and other connective-tissue loads sit relative to your usual training history.
Training load and purpose are distinguished across matches, lessons, footwork, and technical training.
The app separately tracks fatigue from high-force work, whole-body load, specific muscles, high-speed movements, and reactive movements.
Fatigue is separated into five dimensions
See which muscles currently have relatively more residual fatigue.
Build a plan around your available days and time, required exercises, and excluded exercises.
Loaded exercises, pull-ups, push-ups, and planks are calculated according to the characteristics of each exercise.
See relative trends in training load that may remain in joints, tendons, ligaments, and other connective tissues.
Turn workout records into analysis and planning
WhatYouGottaDo uses your strength-training and badminton records to analyze current fatigue and training balance and help you plan what to do next.
App scores do not represent injury probability or the amount of tissue damage. They are relative metrics for tracking how fatigue and training load change within your own records.
Prioritize actual symptoms such as pain or instability over app scores.
This app uses multiple calculation protocols to transform workout records into comparable metrics.
Fatigue and connective-tissue scores do not represent diagnoses, injury probability, tissue damage, or an exact time when recovery will be complete.
The app does not claim medical accuracy
Open the explanation of calculation principles and limitations
Some calculations use findings directly supported by research, while others use practical product policies and heuristics based on relevant research and exercise characteristics.
Research and product policies are both used
The public protocol documentation describes the current formulas, evidence levels, implementation status, and known limitations.
Calculation methods and limitations are documented
